title: A low-loss dielectric filling WR-90, 100 W at 10 GHz: the heat it absorbs and the temperature it reaches, the walls a 20 °C sink
source: A matched line of a low-loss dielectric (εr = 2.2, tan δ = 0.002, k = 0.25 W/(m·K)) filling 30 mm of WR-90, 100 W incident at 10 GHz: it absorbs P(1 − e^{−2αL}) = 2.0579 W (α of γ = √((π/a)² − k0² εr(1 − j tan δ)), D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §3.3), deposited as q = ½ωε₀ε″|E|² = q₀ sin²(πx/a), |E₀|² = 4Z_TE P/(ab). With the walls a sink and the attenuation over the line small (e^{−2αL} = 0.98), the temperature solves −k∇²T = q̄ sin²(πx/a) on the a × b section, q̄ the mean over the length, T = 0 on its sides (Zienkiewicz & Taylor's heat conduction): by the double sine series (m odd to 79, n odd to 399), the rise at the centre is 23.18 K. Evaluated separately from EMCraft's code
